$comment: Estimated orientation of each raw generated Triassic body, read off fixed-world-axis renders
(tools/triassic/preview-orient.py) rather than guessed from the mesh. `yaw` is the rotation in
degrees about +y that brings the animal's head round to +z, which is where every shipped body
keeps it: nothosaurus carries anchor_mouth at z +2.73 of a 5.26 extent, coccosteus at +1.83 of
4.45. Up is +y in every one of these files, so no pitch or roll is estimated.
These are ESTIMATES for previewing and nothing else. They are not a substitute for the
orientation and scale normalization the pipeline does when a body is cleaned and rigged, and
tools/triassic/preview-bodies.mjs deletes the whole preview entry the day the real body ships.
A yaw here that turns out wrong costs a preview that faces the wrong way, never a shipped asset.
